members.name: Bramwell Ashdown
members.role: Master woodcutter at the Ferncross; fells oak and ash for Elmwick and Reedmoor, and keeps the charcoal pits on the side.
ties: husband of Nesta Ashdown
father of Corliss Ashdown
sells timber to Hob Garrow and Nell Sedge
owes Alder Rush of Fernhollow a share of charcoal for last winter's grain
grudges the Coldwell outlaws for stolen tools
friendly with Orvin Hollis of Sootwood

members.name: Nesta Ashdown
members.role: Keeps the Ferncross kitchen and the common pot for the woodcutters; trades bread and broth for fish and fibre.
ties: wife of Bramwell Ashdown
mother of Corliss Ashdown
trades bread with Tansy Sedge and Thistle Mossfoot
close with Maren Hollis of Sootwood
worries about the winter store

members.name: Corliss Ashdown
members.role: Bramwell and Nesta's daughter; stacks kindling and learns the axe and the charcoal burn.
ties: daughter of Bramwell Ashdown and Nesta Ashdown
plays with Fennel Underbank when Fernhollow folk come
wants to see the quay at Lanternquay
afraid of the wolves that come down the wood road

members.name: Odelia Harrow
members.role: A woodcutter who works the south side of the crossing, trimming and hauling; keeps the tally of loads.
ties: wife of Roderick Harrow
mother of Tamsin Harrow
works alongside Bramwell Ashdown
trades timber with Elmwick builders
owes Nell Sedge a share of a load for the Lakemead fence
friendly with Rill Fenlake of the Lakemead

members.name: Roderick Harrow
members.role: Farms the small clearing by the crossing: barley, roots and a few goats; sells grain to the woodcutters and the Fernhollow pedlar.
ties: husband of Odelia Harrow
father of Tamsin Harrow
sells barley to Nesta Ashdown's kitchen
trades seeds with Merrow Stave of Thornby
owes Alder Rush of Fernhollow for a loan of grain
grudges the Kettlebridge works for the smoke that drifts east

members.name: Tamsin Harrow
members.role: Odelia and Roderick's daughter; helps with the goats and the garden, and follows her mother into the woods.
ties: daughter of Odelia Harrow and Roderick Harrow
plays with Corliss Ashdown
afraid of the deep woods and the wolves

situations.summary: Bramwell Ashdown owes Alder Rush of Fernhollow a share of charcoal from last winter's burn, and the share has not been delivered because the pits burned slow and the Elmwick order came first.

sides.Bramwell Ashdown: Knows he owes the charcoal and means to pay, but the Elmwick timber order pays marks now and Alder can wait; feels the pinch of a bad burn and does not want to be thought a poor debtor.
sides.Alder Rush: Knows the charcoal is owed and has asked for it twice; needs it for the hollow's common store before winter and is starting to think Bramwell puts Elmwick first.

situations.summary: The Ferncross households' winter store is thinner than usual: Roderick Harrow's barley came in light and Nesta Ashdown's kitchen is feeding more woodcutters than the plot can carry, so the two houses are sharing out what they have and watching the weather.

sides.Nesta Ashdown: Knows the kitchen store is low and feels responsible for feeding whoever comes to the crossing; wants Roderick to sell her more barley on credit and fears he will not.
sides.Roderick Harrow: Knows his barley was light and feels the shame of a poor harvest; wants to keep enough seed for spring and is torn between helping Nesta and protecting his own house.
sides.Odelia Harrow: Knows the store is short and has offered to trade a load of timber to Elmwick for grain; feels her husband is too proud to ask for help and her neighbour too anxious to wait.

situations.summary: Odelia Harrow sold Elmwick timber for the Lakemead fence last month, and Nell Sedge of Reedmoor has heard of it and says Ferncross is taking sides in the Lakemead quarrel; Odelia says a sale is a sale.

sides.Odelia Harrow: Knows she sold the timber and feels the sale was honest work; resents being told who she may sell to and thinks Nell Sedge is making a quarrel out of a fence post.
sides.Nell Sedge: Knows Elmwick pulled down the Lakemead fence twice and feels Ferncross should not arm either side; wants an apology or a promise of no more timber to Elmwick's fence, and is ready to hold back Reedmoor's fish trade to get it.
sides.Bramwell Ashdown: Knows the sale happened and feels caught between his wife's trade and Reedmoor's custom; wants the quarrel to blow over before it costs the crossing its fish.
